extracted.intended_audience: law students and instructors studying or teaching patent drafting and prosecution (also useful for patent bar candidates)
extracted.subtask_description: Syllabus-level curriculum for a law-school course teaching how to draft patent specifications and claims and to prosecute applications before the USPTO, including practical exercises and patent-bar preparation. Covers claim anatomy and choices, specification components, prosecution strategy, industry-specific issues, and capstone practical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomy of a Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Introductory phrase / preamble; Transitional phrase ("comprising," "consisting of," etc.); Body / elements; Multiple types: independent, dependent, multiple dependent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand and teach the distinct structural parts of a claim and the available claim types; emphasize correct use of preambles and transitional language to control scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Drafting Choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Open vs. closed transitions; Means-plus-function vs. structural; Method vs. apparatus vs. system; Genus vs. species; Markush groupings; Negative limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight the strategic tradeoffs among drafting options (scope, prosecution and enforcement risks, indefiniteness/§112 issues). Practice choosing transitions and claim formats appropriate to disclosure and enforcement goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification Drafting (required components)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification encompasses drawings, written description, and claims: Title of invention; Cross-reference to related applications; Statement regarding federally sponsored research; Background of the invention; Brief summary; Brief description of drawings; Detailed description; Claims; Abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach how each element supports claim scope and §112 requirements (written description/enablement), and how to draft statements (e.g., cross-refs, government support) that comply with procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capstone / Practical Exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Students typically draft a complete patent application; practice claim drafting exercises; respond to mock office actions; conduct prior art search; draft licensing agreements; present patent strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hands-on projects to integrate drafting and prosecution skills; include simulated prosecution and client-facing tasks (licensing, strategy presentation) to mirror practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Bar Exam Preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Most programs prepare students for the USPTO Registration Examination ("Patent Bar") with heavy MPEP focus, patent prosecution rules and procedures, and practice questions on actual patent application elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize mastery of MPEP rules and practical application of prosecution procedures via practice questions modeled on real application elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Office action responses; Interview practice; Continuation strategy; After-final practice; Appeals (PTAB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach tactical prosecution decisions (e.g., when to interview, continuation practice, after-final options, and PTAB appeal practice) and developing a prosecution strategy aligned with client goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Law and Policy Topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Constitutional/statutory basis; Enforcement mechanisms; Patent reform debates; International harmonization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover doctrinal and policy context to inform drafting and prosecution choices; discuss how legal developments and reform debates (and international differences) affect practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-Specific Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Pharma/biotech (Hatch-Waxman, BPCIA, ANDA); Software (Alice/Mayo, copyright overlap); Mechanical/electrical; Standard-essential patents (FRAND).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address sector-specific laws and case law that affect claim drafting and prosecution strategy; tailor exercises to domain-specific issues (e.g., enablement in biotech, eligibility in software, SEP licensing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical Skills Emphasized
rubrics_metrics.description: Reading patents critically; Evaluating prior art; Understanding examiner mindset; Working with inventors (interviewing for invention disclosure); Drafting for litigation defense; International filing strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop practitioner-oriented skills: critical patent analysis, prior art searching, inventor interviews to capture adequate disclosure, drafting choices to withstand litigation, and planning international filings.
